chunks: Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim al-Darimi narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, that Ali عليه السلام said:
Regarding the reward for the runaway slave: “Indeed, the Muslim is returned to the Muslim.”

key_terms.الْآبِقِ: A runaway slave who has fled from his master.
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمَ: The Muslim; here referring to the person to be returned.
key_terms.جُعْلِ: A reward, compensation, or assigned payment for performing a task.
key_terms.غِيَاثُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: A narrator in the sanad of this hadith.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali عليه السلام say about the ruling on returning a runaway slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the case of an absconding slave and the matter of compensation or reward related to returning him. Imam Ali عليه السلام states that the Muslim is to be returned to the Muslim, indicating the obligation of restoring such a person to his owner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3539 - Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim al-Darimi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said regarding the reward for capturing a runaway slave:
"Indeed, the Muslim should be returned to the Muslim."
